# Subagent-Driven Development

Execute plan by dispatching fresh subagent per task, with two-stage review after each: spec compliance review first, then code quality review.

**Core principle:** Fresh subagent per task + two-stage review (spec then quality) = high quality, fast iteration

## When to Use

```dot

    "Have implementation plan?" [shape=diamond];
    "Tasks mostly independent?" [shape=diamond];

    "Have implementation plan?" -> "Manual execution or brainstorm first" [label="no"];
    "Tasks mostly independent?" -> "Stay in this session?" [label="yes"];

    "Stay in this session?" -> "subagent-driven-development" [label="yes"];
    "Stay in this session?" -> "executing-plans" [label="no - parallel session"];
}
```

**vs. Executing Plans (parallel session):**
- Same session (no context switch)
- Fresh subagent per task (no context pollution)
- Two-stage review after each task: spec compliance first, then code quality
- Faster iteration (no human-in-loop between tasks)

## The Process

```dot

    rankdir=TB;

    subgraph cluster_per_task {
        label="Per Task";
        "Dispatch implementer subagent (./implementer-prompt.md)" [shape=box];

    "More tasks remain?" [shape=diamond];
    "Dispatch final code reviewer subagent for entire implementation" [shape=box];
    "Use superpowers:finishing-a-development-branch" [shape=box style=filled fillcolor=lightgreen];

    "Read plan, extract all tasks with full text, note context, create TodoWrite" -> "Dispatch implementer subagent (./implementer-prompt.md)";

    "Implementer subagent implements, tests, commits, self-reviews" -> "Dispatch spec reviewer subagent (./spec-reviewer-prompt.md)";
    "Dispatch spec reviewer subagent (./spec-reviewer-prompt.md)" -> "Spec reviewer subagent confirms code matches spec?";
    "Spec reviewer subagent confirms code matches spec?" -> "Implementer subagent fixes spec gaps" [label="no"];

```

## Prompt Templates

- `./implementer-prompt.md` - Dispatch implementer subagent
- `./spec-reviewer-prompt.md` - Dispatch spec compliance reviewer subagent
- `./code-quality-reviewer-prompt.md` - Dispatch code quality reviewer subagent

## Example Workflow

```
You: I'm using Subagent-Driven Development to execute this plan.

[Read plan file once: docs/plans/feature-plan.md]
[Extract all 5 tasks with full text and context]
[Create TodoWrite with all tasks]

Task 1: Hook installation script

[Get Task 1 text and context (already extracted)]
[Dispatch implementation subagent with full task text + context]

Implementer: "Before I begin - should the hook be installed at user or system level?"

You: "User level (~/.config/superpowers/hooks/)"

Implementer: "Got it. Implementing now..."
[Later] Implementer:
  - Implemented install-hook command
  - Added tests, 5/5 passing
  - Self-review: Found I missed --force flag, added it
  - Committed

[Dispatch spec compliance reviewer]
Spec reviewer: ✅ Spec compliant - all requirements met, nothing extra

[Get git SHAs, dispatch code quality reviewer]
Code reviewer: Strengths: Good test coverage, clean. Issues: None. Approved.

[Mark Task 1 complete]

Task 2: Recovery modes

[Get Task 2 text and context (already extracted)]
[Dispatch implementation subagent with full task text + context]

Implementer: [No questions, proceeds]
Implementer:
  - Added verify/repair modes
  - 8/8 tests passing
  - Self-review: All good
  - Committed

[Dispatch spec compliance reviewer]
Spec reviewer: ❌ Issues:
  - Missing: Progress reporting (spec says "report every 100 items")
  - Extra: Added --json flag (not requested)

[Implementer fixes issues]
Implementer: Removed --json flag, added progress reporting

[Spec reviewer reviews again]
Spec reviewer: ✅ Spec compliant now

[Dispatch code quality reviewer]
Code reviewer: Strengths: Solid. Issues (Important): Magic number (100)

[Implementer fixes]
Implementer: Extracted PROGRESS_INTERVAL constant

[Code reviewer reviews again]
Code reviewer: ✅ Approved

[Mark Task 2 complete]

...

[After all tasks]
[Dispatch final code-reviewer]
Final reviewer: All requirements met, ready to merge

Done!
```

## Advantages

**vs. Manual execution:**
- Subagents follow TDD naturally
- Fresh context per task (no confusion)
- Parallel-safe (subagents don't interfere)
- Subagent can ask questions (before AND during work)

**vs. Executing Plans:**
- Same session (no handoff)
- Continuous progress (no waiting)
- Review checkpoints automatic

**Efficiency gains:**
- No file reading overhead (controller provides full text)
- Controller curates exactly what context is needed
- Subagent gets complete information upfront
- Questions surfaced before work begins (not after)

**Quality gates:**
- Self-review catches issues before handoff
- Two-stage review: spec compliance, then code quality
- Review loops ensure fixes actually work
- Spec compliance prevents over/under-building
- Code quality ensures implementation is well-built

**Cost:**
- More subagent invocations (implementer + 2 reviewers per task)
- Controller does more prep work (extracting all tasks upfront)
- Review loops add iterations
- But catches issues early (cheaper than debugging later)

## Red Flags

**Never:**
- Start implementation on main/master branch without explicit user consent
- Skip reviews (spec compliance OR code quality)
- Proceed with unfixed issues
- Dispatch multiple implementation subagents in parallel (conflicts)
- Make subagent read plan file (provide full text instead)
- Skip scene-setting context (subagent needs to understand where task fits)
- Ignore subagent questions (answer before letting them proceed)
- Accept "close enough" on spec compliance (spec reviewer found issues = not done)
- Skip review loops (reviewer found issues = implementer fixes = review again)
- Let implementer self-review replace actual review (both are needed)
- **Start code quality review before spec compliance is ✅** (wrong order)
- Move to next task while either review has open issues

**If subagent asks questions:**
- Answer clearly and completely
- Provide additional context if needed
- Don't rush them into implementation

**If reviewer finds issues:**
- Implementer (same subagent) fixes them
- Reviewer reviews again
- Repeat until approved
- Don't skip the re-review

**If subagent fails task:**
- Dispatch fix subagent with specific instructions
- Don't try to fix manually (context pollution)

## Integration

**Required workflow skills:**
- **superpowers:using-git-worktrees** - REQUIRED: Set up isolated workspace before starting
- **superpowers:writing-plans** - Creates the plan this skill executes
- **superpowers:requesting-code-review** - Code review template for reviewer subagents
- **superpowers:finishing-a-development-branch** - Complete development after all tasks

**Subagents should use:**
- **superpowers:test-driven-development** - Subagents follow TDD for each task

**Alternative workflow:**
- **superpowers:executing-plans** - Use for parallel session instead of same-session execution

You are implementing Task 1.1: Initialize Next.js 15 Project

## Task Description

Scaffold a Next.js 15 project in /home/dev/vibe with TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, ESLint, and App Router.

**IMPORTANT:** The directory /home/dev/vibe already contains files that must be preserved:
- `BUILD_LOG.md`
- `CLAUDE.md`
- `.claude/` directory
- `docs/` directory (with plans inside)
- `notebooklm-content/` directory

**Steps:**

1. Create the Next.js project in a temporary directory:
```bash
cd /tmp && npx create-next-app@15 vibe-scaffold --typescript --tailwind --eslint --app --no-src-dir --turbopack --import-alias "@/*" --yes
```

2. Copy scaffold files into the real project directory (without overwriting existing files):
```bash
# Copy package.json, tsconfig.json, next.config files, etc.
cp /tmp/vibe-scaffold/package.json /home/dev/vibe/
cp /tmp/vibe-scaffold/tsconfig.json /home/dev/vibe/
cp /tmp/vibe-scaffold/next.config.ts /home/dev/vibe/ 2>/dev/null || cp /tmp/vibe-scaffold/next.config.mjs /home/dev/vibe/ 2>/dev/null || true
cp /tmp/vibe-scaffold/postcss.config.mjs /home/dev/vibe/ 2>/dev/null || true
cp /tmp/vibe-scaffold/.eslintrc.json /home/dev/vibe/ 2>/dev/null || true
cp -r /tmp/vibe-scaffold/app /home/dev/vibe/
cp -r /tmp/vibe-scaffold/public /home/dev/vibe/ 2>/dev/null || true
cp /tmp/vibe-scaffold/.gitignore /home/dev/vibe/
```

3. Install dependencies in the real project:
```bash
cd /home/dev/vibe && npm install
```

4. Install additional dependencies:
```bash
cd /home/dev/vibe && npm install motion howler clsx
npm install -D @types/howler
```

5. Update next.config to be simple and clean:
```typescript
// next.config.ts or next.config.mjs
const nextConfig = {
  reactStrictMode: true,
  eslint: {
    ignoreDuringBuilds: true,
  },
  typescript: {
    ignoreBuildErrors: true,
  },
  images: {
    unoptimized: true,
  },
}
export default nextConfig
```

6. Verify the dev server starts:
```bash
cd /home/dev/vibe && npm run dev
```
The server should start successfully on localhost:3000. Kill it after verifying.

7. Initialize git repo and create initial commit:
```bash
cd /home/dev/vibe
git init
git add package.json tsconfig.json next.config.* postcss.config.* .eslintrc.* .gitignore app/ public/ node_modules/.package-lock.json
git add BUILD_LOG.md CLAUDE.md docs/ .claude/
# Do NOT add node_modules
git commit -m "chore: scaffold Next.js 15 project with TypeScript and Tailwind v4

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>"
```

8. Clean up temp scaffold:
```bash
rm -rf /tmp/vibe-scaffold
```

## Context

This is the foundation for Vibe Voyager, an interactive space exploration game teaching agentic AI concepts. Everything in subsequent phases depends on this scaffold being correct. The project must use:
- Next.js 15 (stable) with App Router
- TypeScript
- Tailwind CSS v4 (CSS-first config with @import "tailwindcss" and @theme directive)
- NO tailwind.config.js (Tailwind v4 uses CSS-first configuration)

## Your Job

1. Execute the steps above
2. Verify the project runs (dev server starts)
3. Commit the work
4. Report back with what was created and any issues

Work from: /home/dev/vibe

**Critical:** Do NOT delete or overwrite BUILD_LOG.md, CLAUDE.md, .claude/, docs/, or notebooklm-content/. These are existing project files that must be preserved.

# Vibe Voyager — Project CLAUDE.md

## Project
Interactive space exploration game teaching vibe coding, agentic AI, and modern SE practices.
URL: [REDACTED_DOMAIN] | Hosting: Vercel free tier | Deadline: ~2026-03-14

## Stack
- Next.js 15, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS v4 (@import "tailwindcss", @theme directive)
- Motion (`motion` package, import from `motion/react` — NOT framer-motion)
- HTML5 Canvas (star map, mini-games)
- Howler.js (ambient audio + SFX sprites)
- localStorage (game save state — no backend)

## Design System
- Style: Clean minimalist sci-fi (glassmorphism, parallax, SVG planets)
- Void: #0a0f1a | Nebula Blue: #4a6fa5 | Signal Green: #6b9e78
- Core Terracotta: #c17147 | Starlight: #e8e0d4 | Glass: rgba(255,255,255,0.05)
- Fonts: Space Grotesk (display), Inter (body), JetBrains Mono (code)
- Panels: backdrop-blur + thin border glow. Framer spring animations on all transitions.

## Key Files
- `BUILD_LOG.md` — Update after every major milestone (tracks build process for meta section)
- `sources.md` — 57+ curated links, primary content source
- Memory files at `~/.claude/projects/-Users-shehral-vibe/memory/` — consult before each session

## Memory References
- `memory/project-overview.md` — narrative arc, audience, metaphors
- `memory/tech-stack.md` — full stack details, colors, typography
- `memory/game-systems.md` — stats, ranks, missions, crew, inventory
- `memory/content-mapping.md` — every planet, every mission, content sources
- `memory/user-preferences.md` — build style, hosting, timeline

## Game Structure
3 Acts + Epilogue. 8 planets. 34 missions. 5 crew members. 4 player stats. 10 Academy sections.
See memory/game-systems.md and memory/content-mapping.md for full details.

## Rules
- ALWAYS check context7 for latest Motion/Next.js/Tailwind v4 APIs before writing components.
- All game state in localStorage — no backend, no database, no auth.
- Academy section accessible from title screen WITHOUT playing the game.
- Update BUILD_LOG.md after completing each major feature (for the meta case study).

# How This Was Built: A Claude Code Case Study

> This document tracks the entire process of building [REDACTED_DOMAIN] using Claude Code with agent teams, plugins, and skills. It serves as both a behind-the-scenes look and living proof of the agentic development practices taught on the platform.

## Build Metadata
- **Start Date:** 2026-03-07

'use client'

import { useState } from 'react'
import { motion, AnimatePresence } from 'motion/react'
import { useRouter } from 'next/navigation'
import { StarfieldBackground, GlassPanel, TypewriterText, Button } from '@/components/ui'
import { useGame } from '@/lib/game-context'
import { ShipType } from '@/lib/types'

  const [step, setStep] = useState(1)
  const [callsign, setCallsign] = useState('')
  const [ship, setShip] = useState<ShipType>('spark')
  const { startNewGame } = useGame()
  const router = useRouter()

  const isValidCallsign = callsign.trim().length >= 2 && callsign.length <= 20

  const handleLaunch = () => {
    startNewGame(callsign.trim(), ship)
    router.push('/cockpit')
  }

  // ... render with AnimatePresence switching on step
}
```

```css
/* Add to the component or use inline styles */

  perspective: 300px;
  overflow: hidden;
  height: 60vh;
}
.text-crawl {
  transform: rotateX(20deg);
  animation: crawl 30s linear infinite;
}
@keyframes crawl {
  from { transform: rotateX(20deg) translateY(100%); }
  to { transform: rotateX(20deg) translateY(-100%); }
}
```
Alternatively, use a simpler vertical scroll with opacity fade at top/bottom.
